title: The women who followed from Galilee — at the cross, at the burial, and first at the empty tomb (Luke 8; John 20; Deuteronomy 19)
summary:
It ain't new. The same women are at every station. They had followed him from Galilee and kept him out of their own means:

*And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils,* (Luke 8:2)

*And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance.* (Luke 8:3)

They stood at the cross when the twelve were gone:

*And many women were there beholding afar off, which followed Yahusha (Jesus) from Galilee, ministering unto him:* (Matthew 27:55)

*Among which was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s children.* (Matthew 27:56)

*Now there stood by the cross of Yahusha (Jesus) his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.* (John 19:25)

They sat at the burial:

*And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.* (Matthew 27:61)

And they came first to the tomb and were the first told, the first sent, and the first he met:

*In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1)

*And go quickly, and tell his disciples that he is risen from the dead; and, behold, he goeth before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him: lo, I have told you.* (Matthew 28:7)

*And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Yahusha (Jesus) met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.* (Matthew 28:9)

*Then said Yahusha (Jesus) unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.* (Matthew 28:10)

Mark says it outright, and John tells what Mary was given to carry:

*Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils.* (Mark 16:9)

*Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my Elohim (God), and your Elohim (God).* (John 20:17)

*Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen Yahusha (Lord), and that he had spoken these things unto her.* (John 20:18)

*Go tell my brethren*: the first witness of the rising is a woman carrying the word to the men. The Torah establishes a matter at the mouth of two or three witnesses, and there were two Marys at the tomb, the same two who had sat at the grave and stood at the cross:

*One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sinneth: at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established.* (Deuteronomy 19:15)

Who can find such a woman, the proverb asks, and the gospels answer with names: Mary Magdalene, the other Mary, Joanna, Susanna, and many others, who saw the death, the burial and the empty grave with their own eyes and were believed by the brethren because they were sent.

*Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.* (Proverbs 31:10)

3227.prose: The two who came at dawn are not strangers. Matthew has already told us there were many women at the cross, watching from far off, and they had come *from Galilee*. The women at the tomb are the same women who stayed when the twelve were gone.
3227.phrase: many women were there beholding afar off
3227.sentence: The many women watching from far off are the ones who then come to the sepulchre at first light.

3228.prose: Before they came to the tomb they sat at it. The two Marys were *sitting over against the sepulchre* and watched where he was laid. So when they come at first light, they come knowing the place, having seen the burial with their own eyes.
3228.phrase: Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre
3228.sentence: The same two who come at dawn were there at the burial, watching the grave and knowing the place.

3216.prose: The same morning from the women's side. The sabbath was past and they had *bought sweet spices* to anoint a body they took to be still in the grave. Matthew gives the hour, Mark gives the errand, and both have the same faithful women walking to the same tomb.
3216.phrase: had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him
3216.sentence: The women arrive with bought spices and a purpose, which gives Matthew's two Marys their errand at the sepulchre.

3217.prose: Luke gives the same dawn. They came on the first day, *very early in the morning*, carrying spices they had made ready beforehand. Matthew's women and Luke's are the same faithful witnesses, walking to a tomb they expected to find shut with him inside it.
3217.phrase: they came unto the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared
3217.sentence: Luke shows the women bringing prepared spices with others beside them, the company Matthew's two Marys belong to.

3229.prose: John stays with Mary. She *stood without at the sepulchre weeping* once the men had gone home, and she stooped down to look in. The one who came at dawn is the one who will not leave, and she is the one Yahusha (Jesus) speaks to first.
3229.phrase: Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping
3229.sentence: Mary stays at the grave weeping and looks in, the same woman who came with the others at dawn.

3230.prose: John names the women at the cross, *his mother* among them, then Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene. Mary Magdalene is there again. The one who stands at the cross is the one who comes at dawn to the grave.
3230.phrase: Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene
3230.sentence: Mary Magdalene is named among the women standing at the cross, the same woman who comes to the sepulchre.

3231.prose: The proverb asks *who can find a virtuous woman*, and Matthew answers with names. Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to the grave while it was still dawning. Their *price is far above rubies*, and they are found where the faithful are found, at the place everyone else left.
3231.phrase: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies
3231.sentence: The proverb's question is answered by named women who were found at the grave when others had gone.

3232.prose: Luke begins the story of how they came to be there. He went *throughout every city and village*, and the twelve were with him, and the next lines name the women who were with them too, Mary called Magdalene and others. They followed from the first, long before the cross.
3232.phrase: went throughout every city and village, preaching and shewing the glad tidings
3232.sentence: The women who stand at the tomb had travelled with him through every city and village from the start.

7123.prose: Luke says *they came unto the sepulchre* and leaves most of them unnamed. Matthew names the two at the front, *Mary Magdalene and the other Mary*. Put together, the company Luke describes had these two leading it, and they are the same two who sat at the grave.
7123.phrase: came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre
7123.sentence: Matthew puts names to the company Luke leaves unnamed: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary.

5358.prose: Mark names the women watching from far off. Matthew says who they were to him: they had *followed* him *from Galilee*, and they were *ministering unto him* the whole way. These are not onlookers from the crowd. They are the ones who kept him.
5358.phrase: which followed Yahusha (Jesus) from Galilee, ministering unto him
5358.sentence: The women Mark names at the cross had followed Yahusha (Jesus) from Galilee and served him.

5359.prose: Luke puts it plainly: *all his acquaintance*, and *the women that followed him from Galilee*, stood far off and watched. Mark names three of them, and Luke tells us they had followed from Galilee too. Same women, same place, seen from another side.
5359.phrase: the women that followed him from Galilee, stood afar off, beholding these things
5359.sentence: Luke says the women who followed from Galilee stood at a distance and watched, as Mark has them.

5360.prose: John brings the women right up to the cross. *Mary Magdalene* is there again, with the mother of Yahusha (Jesus) and her sister. Mark has them at a distance. John says they *stood by the cross*. They stayed close to the end.
5360.phrase: Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene
5360.sentence: John lists Mary Magdalene among the women standing at the cross, close to where Mark has them watching.

5363.prose: Mark has the women coming with spices to anoint him. Matthew gives the hour, *as it began to dawn*, and says they came *to see the sepulchre*. Two accounts, one dawn, the same two Marys walking to the grave.
5363.phrase: as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week
5363.sentence: Matthew gives the dawn hour at which Mark's women come to the grave, with Mary Magdalene and the other Mary named.

5364.prose: Luke shows the spices in their hands. They came *very early in the morning*, *bringing the spices*, and *certain others* with them. The errand Mark gives is carried out, and more women walk with the three he names.
5364.phrase: bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them
5364.sentence: Luke shows the errand Mark names being carried out, with other women beside the ones named.

5365.prose: John follows Mary Magdalene alone, *early, when it was yet dark*. Mark has her with the others and the spices. John has her seeing *the stone taken away* and running with the news. Whoever else is with her, she is the one who is there first.
5365.phrase: Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre
5365.sentence: John shows Mary Magdalene at the sepulchre in the dark, the first to see the stone moved.

5370.prose: Mark tells how they trembled. Matthew shows the same fear and says it came with *great joy*, so they *did run to bring his disciples word*. Fear is in both accounts, and in Matthew it does not keep them from the errand they were sent on.
5370.phrase: departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy
5370.sentence: Matthew keeps the women's fear but joins it to joy and a run to carry the word to the disciples.

5372.prose: Mark says he appeared first to Mary Magdalene. Matthew shows the meeting. As they went, Yahusha (Jesus) *met them*, and they *held him by the feet, and worshipped him*. The first to be seen by him are the women, and they take hold of him and worship.
5372.phrase: they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him
5372.sentence: Matthew shows the women meeting the risen Yahusha (Jesus), taking hold of his feet and worshipping.

5371.prose: Mark says he appeared first to Mary Magdalene. John shows how it went. She *stood without at the sepulchre weeping* and stooped to look in, and it is to her that Yahusha (Jesus) then speaks and sends. The first to be seen is the woman who would not leave the grave.
5371.phrase: as she wept, she stooped down, and looked into the sepulchre
5371.sentence: John shows Mary weeping at the empty tomb and looking in, the woman Mark says he appeared to first.
